newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's centre-right says will not vote on budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's centre-right says will not vote on budget.

text.p: Italian centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said on Monday the Freedom Alliance would not participate in voting on the 1997 draft budget in the lower house of parliament.

"Being put in the position of it being impossible for us to carry out our rights and duties as the opposition, we will not participate in voting on the budget law," Berlusconi said in the full house of the Chamber of Deputies (lower house).
Berlusconi, who met other Freedom Alliance leaders for an hour and a half on Monday morning, accuses the government of not allowing full debate of the budget measures.

The government wants to push through certain aspects of the draft legislation using special proxy powers which by-pass parliament by removing the need for parliamentary approval of the specific details.

But the absence of the Freedom Alliance from voting on the budget package, which aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire from Italy's budget defcit next year, will not leave the lower house inquorate, political sources said.
If the hard-left Communist Refoundation party votes with the centre-left government, the 1997 budget legislation can still have a smooth passage through the lower house, they added.
